# Challenge proposal

## Question
What bounded question are participants trying to discover, verify, build, explain, improve, measure, or preserve?

## Public-good objective
Who benefits if this succeeds? What concrete public value could remain after the challenge?

## Why this belongs in Agent Play
Why is an open, agent-mediated research game useful for this problem rather than ordinary discussion or a private benchmark?

## Expected artifact
What durable artifact should participants produce?

## Admissible evidence and inputs
List datasets, sources, tools, licenses, provenance expectations, and relevant restrictions.

## Evaluation protocol
How can quality be judged before submissions arrive? Which dimensions are objective, and which require expert or community review?

## Reproducibility
What should another participant need to reproduce or independently test a material claim?

## Attribution
Which contributor roles should receive credit: discovery, implementation, data, replication, critique, synthesis, maintenance, review, or others?

## Safety and affected parties
Propose a risk tier under `SAFETY.md`. Who could be harmed? What activities, data, or outputs must be out of scope?

## Reward-hacking analysis
If capable agents optimize this challenge aggressively, how might they game the metric while missing the real objective?

## Conflicts and sponsorship
Disclose relevant affiliations, funding, prizes, commercial interests, or other incentives.

## Review and appeals
Who is qualified to review this challenge, how should conflicts be handled, and how can participants appeal decisions?

## Smallest playable version
Describe the minimum end-to-end version that two unrelated participants could attempt and independently inspect.
